change: Secondary muscles revised: replaced 'Posterior Deltoid' with 'Anterior Deltoids' (the arm swings forward/overhead during the recovery phase, not into rear-delt extension); added 'mid back' (Rhomboids + Lower Traps) for scapular stabilization confirmed by SkiErg muscle activation sources; added 'Lower Back' (Erector Spinae) for the hip-hinge stabilization inherent to the alternating pull technique. Abs and obliques retained and confirmed by research showing lateral trunk and rotational core demand in the alternating-arm classic technique.

Equipment changed from 'bodyweight' to 'other': skipping uses a jump rope which is external equipment; 'bodyweight' implies no equipment. Added 'abs' (Upper Rectus Abdominis, LowerRectus Abdominis) to secondary: research confirms continuous core stabilization demand during jumping. All other muscles (calves primary; quads, hamstrings, glutes, forearms secondary) confirmed correct.

Added 'oblique' (External Obliques + Internal Obliques) to secondary: per CLAUDE.md rules, unilateral exercises add oblique anti-rotation as secondary; confirmed by sources noting rectus abdominis, obliques, and transverse abdominis engaged for torso stability. Added 'Lower Back' (Erector Spinae) to secondary: core and spinal stabilization confirmed by research. Primary (Quads + glutes) and existing secondary (Hamstrings + Adductors) confirmed correct.

Merged Soleus into primary Calves entry alongside Gastrocnemius Lateral and Gastrocnemius Medial. Removed the duplicate secondary 'Calves' entry containing only Soleus. Rationale: the format rule requires merging one bucket into ONE entry; Soleus activation during standing calf raise is ~45-55% (comparable to gastrocnemius) making it a co-primary mover, not merely secondary. The Smith machine eliminates most stabilizer demand so no meaningful secondary muscles remain.

Merged 'Clavicular Head' from secondary chest entry into the single primary 'chest' entry alongside 'Sternal Head'. The format rule requires one entry per bucket — having chest in both primary and secondary is invalid. Both heads are activated during decline press (sternal dominant); placing both in primary with sternal emphasis correctly represents the anatomy. Triceps Brachii and Anterior Deltoids remain as secondary (confirmed by EMG studies: triceps and anterior deltoid are meaningful secondary movers in all bench press variants, with anterior deltoid less active on decline than incline).
